audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Samuel chapter 19, first-pass draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Joab's coercive response to grief, army shame, political return campaign, Amasa appointment, Shimei's apology and execution proposal, Mephibosheth's accessibility testimony and partial judgment, Barzillai's age and self-assessment, Chimham patronage, tribal rivalry, and threatened renewed fracture.

verses.restored: It was told Joab, Look, king weeps and mourns over Absalom.

familiar.text: And it was told Joab, Behold, the king weepeth and mourneth for Absalom.

modern.text: Then it was reported to Joab, “The king is weeping and mourning over Absalom.”

original.text: וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לְיוֹאָ֑ב הִנֵּ֨ה הַמֶּ֧לֶךְ בֹּכֶ֛ה וַיִּתְאַבֵּ֖ל עַל אַבְשָׁלֹֽם

verses.restored: Rescue/victory on that day became mourning for all people, because people heard that day, King is grieved over his son.

familiar.text: And the victory that day was turned into mourning unto all the people: for the people heard say that day how the king was grieved for his son.

modern.text: And that day’s victory was turned into mourning for all the people, because on that day they were told, “The king is grieving over his son.”

original.text: וַתְּהִ֨י הַתְּשֻׁעָ֜ה בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֛וּא לְאֵ֖בֶל לְכָל הָעָ֑ם כִּֽי שָׁמַ֣ע הָעָ֗ם בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר נֶעֱצַ֥ב הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עַל בְּנֽוֹ

verses.restored: People entered city stealthily that day, as people ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.

familiar.text: And the people gat them by stealth that day into the city, as people being ashamed steal away when they flee in battle.

modern.text: So they returned to the city quietly that day, as people steal away in humiliation after fleeing a battle.

original.text: וַיִּתְגַּנֵּ֥ב הָעָ֛ם בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא לָב֣וֹא הָעִ֑יר כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר יִתְגַּנֵּ֗ב הָעָם֙ הַנִּכְלָמִ֔ים בְּנוּסָ֖ם בַּמִּלְחָמָֽה

verses.restored: King covered his face, and king cried with a great voice, My son Absalom, Absalom my son, my son.

familiar.text: But the king covered his face, and the king cried with a loud voice, O my son Absalom, O Absalom, my son, my son!

modern.text: But the king covered his face and cried out at the top of his voice, “O my son Absalom! O Absalom, my son, my son!”

original.text: וְהַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לָאַ֣ט אֶת פָּנָ֔יו וַיִּזְעַ֥ק הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ ק֣וֹל גָּד֑וֹל בְּנִי֙ אַבְשָׁל֔וֹם אַבְשָׁל֖וֹם בְּנִ֥י בְנִֽי

verses.restored: Joab came to king at house and said, Today you have shamed faces of all your servants who rescued your life today, lives of your sons and daughters, lives of your wives, and lives of your concubines.

familiar.text: And Joab came into the house to the king, and said, Thou hast shamed this day the faces of all thy servants, which this day have saved thy life, and the lives of thy sons and of thy daughters, and the lives of thy wives, and the lives of thy concubines;

modern.text: Then Joab went into the house and said to the king, “Today you have disgraced all your servants who have saved your life and the lives of your sons and daughters, of your wives, and of your concubines.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֥א יוֹאָ֛ב אֶל הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ הַבָּ֑יִת וַיֹּאמֶר֩ הֹבַ֨שְׁתָּ הַיּ֜וֹם אֶת פְּנֵ֣י כָל עֲבָדֶ֗יךָ הַֽמְמַלְּטִ֤ים אֶֽת נַפְשְׁךָ֙ הַיּ֔וֹם וְאֵ֨ת נֶ֤פֶשׁ בָּנֶ֨יךָ֙ וּבְנֹתֶ֔יךָ וְנֶ֣פֶשׁ נָשֶׁ֔יךָ וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ פִּלַגְשֶֽׁיךָ

verses.restored: By loving those who hate you and hating those who love you, you declared today that commanders and servants are nothing to you. Today I know that if Absalom lived and all of us died, then it would be right in your eyes.

familiar.text: In that thou lovest thine enemies, and hatest thy friends. For thou hast declared this day, that thou regardest neither princes nor servants: for this day I perceive, that if Absalom had lived, and all we had died this day, then it had pleased thee well.

modern.text: You love those who hate you and hate those who love you! For you have made it clear today that the commanders and soldiers mean nothing to you. I know today that if Absalom were alive and all of us were dead, it would have pleased you!

original.text: לְאַֽהֲבָה֙ אֶת שֹׂ֣נְאֶ֔יךָ וְלִשְׂנֹ֖א אֶת אֹהֲבֶ֑יךָ כִּ֣י הִגַּ֣דְתָּ הַיּ֗וֹם כִּ֣י אֵ֤ין לְךָ֙ שָׂרִ֣ים וַעֲבָדִ֔ים כִּ֣י יָדַ֣עְתִּי הַיּ֗וֹם כִּ֠י לא אַבְשָׁל֥וֹם חַי֙ וְכֻלָּ֤נוּ הַיּוֹם֙ מֵתִ֔ים כִּי אָ֖ז יָשָׁ֥ר בְּעֵינֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: Now arise, go out, and speak to heart of your servants. By YHWH I swear, if you do not go out, not a man will remain with you tonight, and this will be worse for you than all evil that came upon you from youth until now.

familiar.text: Now therefore arise, go forth, and speak comfortably unto thy servants: for I swear by the LORD, if thou go not forth, there will not tarry one with thee this night: and that will be worse unto thee than all the evil that befell thee from thy youth until now.

modern.text: Now therefore get up! Go out and speak comfort to your servants, for I swear by the LORD that if you do not go out, not a man will remain with you tonight. This will be worse for you than all the adversity that has befallen you from your youth until now!” David Restored as King

original.text: וְעַתָּה֙ ק֣וּם צֵ֔א וְדַבֵּ֖ר עַל לֵ֣ב עֲבָדֶ֑יךָ כִּי֩ בַיהוָ֨ה נִשְׁבַּ֜עְתִּי כִּי אֵינְךָ֣ יוֹצֵ֗א אִם יָלִ֨ין אִ֤ישׁ אִתְּךָ֙ הַלַּ֔יְלָה וְרָעָ֧ה לְךָ֣ זֹ֗את מִכָּל הָרָעָה֙ אֲשֶׁר בָּ֣אָה עָלֶ֔יךָ מִנְּעֻרֶ֖יךָ עַד עָֽתָּה

verses.restored: King arose and sat in gate. They told all people, saying, Look, king sits in gate. All people came before king. Israel had fled, each to his tent.

familiar.text: Then the king arose, and sat in the gate. And they told unto all the people, saying, Behold, the king doth sit in the gate. And all the people came before the king: for Israel had fled every man to his tent.

modern.text: So the king got up and sat in the gate, and all the people were told: “Behold, the king is sitting in the gate.” So they all came before the king. Meanwhile, the Israelites had fled, each man to his home.

original.text: וַיָּ֥קָם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב בַּשָּׁ֑עַר וּֽלְכָל הָעָ֞ם הִגִּ֣ידוּ לֵאמֹ֗ר הִנֵּ֤ה הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ יוֹשֵׁ֣ב בַּשַּׁ֔עַר וַיָּבֹ֤א כָל הָעָם֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל נָ֖ס אִ֥ישׁ לְאֹהָלָֽיו

verses.restored: All people disputed in all tribes of Israel, saying, King rescued us from hand of enemies and delivered us from hand of Philistines, but now he fled from land before Absalom.

familiar.text: And all the people were at strife throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, The king saved us out of the hand of our enemies, and he delivered us out of the hand of the Philistines; and now he is fled out of the land for Absalom.

modern.text: And all the people throughout the tribes of Israel were arguing, “The king rescued us from the hand of our enemies and delivered us from the hand of the Philistines, but now he has fled the land because of Absalom.

original.text: וַיְהִ֤י כָל הָעָם֙ נָד֔וֹן בְּכָל שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֵאמֹ֑ר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ הִצִּילָ֣נוּ מִכַּ֣ף אֹיְבֵ֗ינוּ וְה֤וּא מִלְּטָ֨נוּ֙ מִכַּ֣ף פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים וְעַתָּ֛ה בָּרַ֥ח מִן הָאָ֖רֶץ מֵעַ֥ל אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם

verses.restored: Absalom, whom we anointed over us, died in battle. Now why are you silent about returning king?

familiar.text: And Absalom, whom we anointed over us, is dead in battle. Now therefore why speak ye not a word of bringing the king back?

modern.text: But Absalom, the man we anointed over us, has died in battle. So why do you say nothing about restoring the king?”

original.text: וְאַבְשָׁלוֹם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָשַׁ֣חְנוּ עָלֵ֔ינוּ מֵ֖ת בַּמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וְעַתָּ֗ה לָמָ֥ה אַתֶּ֛ם מַחֲרִשִׁ֖ים לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: King David sent to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, saying, Speak to elders of Judah: Why are you last to return king to his house, when word of all Israel has come to king at his house?

familiar.text: And king David sent to Zadok and to Abiathar the priests, saying, Speak unto the elders of Judah, saying, Why are ye the last to bring the king back to his house? seeing the speech of all Israel is come to the king, even to his house.

modern.text: Then King David sent this message to Zadok and Abiathar, the priests: “Say to the elders of Judah, ‘Why should you be the last to restore the king to his palace, since the talk of all Israel has reached the king at his quarters?

original.text: וְהַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד שָׁ֠לַח אֶל צָד֨וֹק וְאֶל אֶבְיָתָ֥ר הַכֹּהֲנִים֮ לֵאמֹר֒ דַּבְּר֞וּ אֶל זִקְנֵ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לָ֤מָּה תִֽהְיוּ֙ אַֽחֲרֹנִ֔ים לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל בֵּית֑וֹ וּדְבַר֙ כָּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּ֥א אֶל הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל בֵּיתֽוֹ

verses.restored: You are my brothers; you are my bone and my flesh. Why are you last to return king?

familiar.text: Ye are my brethren, ye are my bones and my flesh: wherefore then are ye the last to bring back the king?

modern.text: You are my brothers, my own flesh and blood. So why should you be the last to restore the king?’

original.text: אַחַ֣י אַתֶּ֔ם עַצְמִ֥י וּבְשָׂרִ֖י אַתֶּ֑ם וְלָ֧מָּה תִהְי֛וּ אַחֲרֹנִ֖ים לְהָשִׁ֥יב אֶת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Say to Amasa, Are you not my bone and flesh? Thus may Divine do to me and thus add if you are not commander of army before me all days in place of Joab.

familiar.text: And say ye to Amasa, Art thou not of my bone, and of my flesh? God do so to me, and more also, if thou be not captain of the host before me continually in the room of Joab.

modern.text: And say to Amasa, ‘Aren’t you my flesh and blood? May God punish me, and ever so severely, if from this time you are not the commander of my army in place of Joab!’”

original.text: וְלַֽעֲמָשָׂא֙ תֹּֽמְר֔וּ הֲל֛וֹא עַצְמִ֥י וּבְשָׂרִ֖י אָ֑תָּה כֹּ֣ה יַֽעֲשֶׂה לִּ֤י אֱלֹהִים֙ וְכֹ֣ה יוֹסִ֔יף אִם לֹ֠א שַׂר צָבָ֞א תִּהְיֶ֧ה לְפָנַ֛י כָּל הַיָּמִ֖ים תַּ֥חַת יוֹאָֽב

verses.restored: He turned heart of every man of Judah as one man, and they sent to king, Return, you and all your servants.

familiar.text: And he bowed the heart of all the men of Judah, even as the heart of one man; so that they sent this word unto the king, Return thou, and all thy servants.

modern.text: So he swayed the hearts of all the men of Judah as though they were one man, and they sent word to the king: “Return, you and all your servants.”

original.text: וַיַּ֛ט אֶת לְבַ֥ב כָּל אִישׁ יְהוּדָ֖ה כְּאִ֣ישׁ אֶחָ֑ד וַֽיִּשְׁלְחוּ֙ אֶל הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שׁ֥וּב אַתָּ֖ה וְכָל עֲבָדֶֽיךָ

verses.restored: King returned and came as far as Jordan. Judah came to Gilgal to meet king, to bring king across Jordan.

familiar.text: So the king returned, and came to Jordan. And Judah came to Gilgal, to go to meet the king, to conduct the king over Jordan.

modern.text: So the king returned, and when he arrived at the Jordan, the men of Judah came to Gilgal to meet him and escort him across the Jordan. Shimei Pardoned

original.text: וַיָּ֣שָׁב הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיָּבֹ֖א עַד הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן וִיהוּדָ֞ה בָּ֣א הַגִּלְגָּ֗לָה לָלֶ֨כֶת֙ לִקְרַ֣את הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ לְהַעֲבִ֥יר אֶת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶת הַיַּרְדֵּֽן

verses.restored: Shimei son of Gera, Benjaminite from Bahurim, hurried and came down with men of Judah to meet king David.

familiar.text: And Shimei the son of Gera, a Benjamite, which was of Bahurim, hasted and came down with the men of Judah to meet king David.

modern.text: Then Shimei son of Gera, a Benjamite from Bahurim, hurried down with the men of Judah to meet King David,

original.text: וַיְמַהֵ֗ר שִׁמְעִ֤י בֶן גֵּרָא֙ בֶּן הַיְמִינִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר מִבַּֽחוּרִ֑ים וַיֵּ֨רֶד֙ עִם אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה לִקְרַ֖את הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִֽד

verses.restored: With him were one thousand men from Benjamin, and Ziba servant of house of Saul with his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They rushed to Jordan before king.

familiar.text: And there were a thousand men of Benjamin with him, and Ziba the servant of the house of Saul, and his fifteen sons and his twenty servants with him; and they went over Jordan before the king.

modern.text: along with a thousand men of Benjamin, as well as Ziba the steward of the house of Saul and his fifteen sons and twenty servants. They rushed down to the Jordan before the king

original.text: וְאֶ֨לֶף אִ֣ישׁ עִמּוֹ֮ מִבִּנְיָמִן֒ וְצִיבָ֗א נַ֚עַר בֵּ֣ית שָׁא֔וּל וַחֲמֵ֨שֶׁת עָשָׂ֥ר בָּנָ֛יו וְעֶשְׂרִ֥ים עֲבָדָ֖יו אִתּ֑וֹ וְצָלְח֥וּ הַיַּרְדֵּ֖ן לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: The crossing service/ferry passed to carry household of king and do what was good in his eyes. Shimei son of Gera fell before king as he crossed Jordan.

familiar.text: And there went over a ferry boat to carry over the king’s household, and to do what he thought good. And Shimei the son of Gera fell down before the king, as he was come over Jordan;

modern.text: and crossed at the ford to carry over the king’s household and to do what was good in his sight. When Shimei son of Gera crossed the Jordan, he fell down before the king

original.text: וְעָבְרָ֣ה הָעֲבָרָ֗ה לַֽעֲבִיר֙ אֶת בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וְלַעֲשׂ֥וֹת הַטּ֖וֹב בעינו וְשִׁמְעִ֣י בֶן גֵּרָ֗א נָפַל֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ בְּעָבְר֖וֹ בַּיַּרְדֵּֽן

verses.restored: He said to king, Do not let my lord reckon guilt to me. Do not remember what your servant did perversely on day my lord king went out from Jerusalem. Do not let king set it on his heart.

familiar.text: And said unto the king, Let not my lord impute iniquity unto me, neither do thou remember that which thy servant did perversely the day that my lord the king went out of Jerusalem, that the king should take it to his heart.

modern.text: and said, “My lord, do not hold me guilty, and do not remember your servant’s wrongdoing on the day my lord the king left Jerusalem. May the king not take it to heart.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ אַל יַחֲשָׁב לִ֣י אֲדֹנִי֮ עָוֺן֒ וְאַל תִּזְכֹּ֗ר אֵ֚ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶעֱוָ֣ה עַבְדְּךָ֔ בַּיּ֕וֹם אֲשֶׁר יָׄצָ֥ׄאׄ אֲדֹנִֽי הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מִירֽוּשָׁלִָ֑ם לָשׂ֥וּם הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶל לִבּֽוֹ

verses.restored: Your servant knows I sinned. Look, I came today first from all house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord king.

familiar.text: For thy servant doth know that I have sinned: therefore, behold, I am come the first this day of all the house of Joseph to go down to meet my lord the king.

modern.text: For your servant knows that I have sinned, so here I am today as the first of all the house of Joseph to come down to meet my lord the king.”

original.text: כִּ֚י יָדַ֣ע עַבְדְּךָ֔ כִּ֖י אֲנִ֣י חָטָ֑אתִי וְהִנֵּֽה בָ֣אתִי הַיּ֗וֹם רִאשׁוֹן֙ לְכָל בֵּ֣ית יוֹסֵ֔ף לָרֶ֕דֶת לִקְרַ֖את אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Abishai son of Zeruiah answered and said, Shall Shimei not be put to death for this, because he cursed anointed of YHWH?

familiar.text: But Abishai the son of Zeruiah answered and said, Shall not Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD’s anointed?

modern.text: But Abishai son of Zeruiah said, “Shouldn’t Shimei be put to death for this, because he cursed the LORD’s anointed?”

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַן אֲבִישַׁ֤י בֶּן צְרוּיָה֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר הֲתַ֣חַת זֹ֔את לֹ֥א יוּמַ֖ת שִׁמְעִ֑י כִּ֥י קִלֵּ֖ל אֶת מְשִׁ֥יחַ יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: David said, What is there to me and to you, sons of Zeruiah, that you become an adversary to me today? Shall any man be put to death today in Israel? Do I not know that today I am king over Israel?

familiar.text: And David said, What have I to do with you, ye sons of Zeruiah, that ye should this day be adversaries unto me? shall there any man be put to death this day in Israel? for do not I know that I am this day king over Israel?

modern.text: And David replied, “Sons of Zeruiah, what have I to do with you, that you should be my adversaries today? Should any man be put to death in Israel today? Am I not indeed aware that today I am king over Israel?”

original.text: וַיַּ֣עַן אִֽישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵל֩ אֶת אִ֨ישׁ יְהוּדָ֜ה וַיֹּ֗אמֶר עֶֽשֶׂר יָד֨וֹת לִ֣י בַמֶּלֶךְ֮ וְגַם בְּדָוִד֮ אֲנִ֣י מִמְּךָ֒ וּמַדּ֨וּעַ֙ הֱקִלֹּתַ֔נִי וְלֹא הָיָ֨ה דְבָרִ֥י רִאשׁ֛וֹן לִ֖י לְהָשִׁ֣יב אֶת מַלְכִּ֑י וַיִּ֨קֶשׁ֙ דְּבַר אִ֣ישׁ יְהוּדָ֔ה מִדְּבַ֖ר אִ֥ישׁ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

translation_notes: Joab responds to David's grief with political threat and shame. A ruler has duties to surviving people, but bereavement does not become illegitimate because it disrupts victory celebration.
The soldiers' lives matter independently of their usefulness to David. Joab's claim that David loves enemies and hates friends simplifies a father's grief into political betrayal.
David uses priests to lobby Judah and offers Amasa Joab's command, blending kinship, patronage, and institutional religious networks in his return campaign.
Shimei apologizes under a thousand-person political delegation. David's refusal to execute him is restraint; 'anointed' language still does not make criticism treason.
Mephibosheth's unkempt body and clothes are signs of mourning/protest, not neglect proving incompetence.
His testimony makes accessibility explicit: he needed a saddled animal, and Ziba controlled the assistance. David again refuses a full hearing and splits property despite conflicting accounts.
Mephibosheth's willingness to surrender all land may reflect relief, dependence, pressure, or rhetorical loyalty; it should not validate the unjust judgment.
Barzillai evaluates his own age, senses, preferences, burial wishes, and travel capacity. His self-description must not become a universal stereotype about older adults.
He declines palace care and chooses home, family grave, and succession support for Chimham. Autonomy includes refusing prestigious arrangements.
The chapter ends in fierce Judah-Israel rivalry, showing that royal restoration did not heal structural division.
safety_note: Do not shame grief, execute critics, or decide disability disputes without accessible testimony and evidence. Do not treat older people as burdens or assume palace care is best. Restored leadership must hear those harmed by its earlier emergency judgments and address regional exclusion before it becomes renewed conflict.
